prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project manages its LTS (Long Term Support) releases by first having an incoming release in a "Current" status, which transitions into an "Active LTS" phase, and finally a "Maintenance LTS" phase before reaching end-of-life. 

Here are the official details regarding the duration of the Active LTS and Maintenance LTS phases:

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-plan | QUOTE: "Active LTS: 18 months" | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase of a Node.js release lasts for 18 months.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-plan | QUOTE: "Maintenance: 12 months" | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase of a Node.js release lasts for 12 months.

*(Note: The official Node.js release repository explains the schedule in further detail by stating that Active LTS begins 6 months after the initial release and Maintenance begins 30 months after the initial release, running until the 42-month mark, which mathematically aligns with the 18-month Active and 12-month Maintenance durations quoted above.)*
